audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Law marriage analogy, Law/sin distinction, commandment, divided I, wretched cry. Preserve Law as holy and sin as parasitic power.

verses.restored: Or do you not know, siblings, for I speak to those knowing Law, that the Law rules over the human for as long a time as one lives?

familiar.text: Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?

verses.restored: For the married woman has been bound by Law to the living husband; but if the husband dies, she has been released from the law of the husband.

familiar.text: For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.

verses.restored: So then, while the husband lives, she will be called adulteress if she comes to another man; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not adulteress, having come to another man.

familiar.text: So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man.

verses.restored: So then, my siblings, you also were put to death to the Law through the body of Messiah, so that you might belong to another, to the one raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit to the Divine.

familiar.text: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.

verses.restored: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins/misalignments through the Law were working in our members to bear fruit to death.

familiar.text: For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.

verses.restored: But now we have been released from the Law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of Spirit and not in oldness of letter.

familiar.text: But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

verses.restored: What then shall we say? Is the Law sin/misalignment? May it not be. But I would not have known sin/misalignment except through Law; for I would not have known desire if the Law had not said, You shall not desire.

familiar.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.

verses.restored: But sin/misalignment, taking opportunity through the commandment, worked in me every desire; for apart from Law, sin/misalignment is dead.

familiar.text: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.

verses.restored: I was once alive apart from Law, but when the commandment came, sin/misalignment came alive,

familiar.text: For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.

verses.restored: and I died; and the commandment that was into life, this was found to be into death for me.

familiar.text: And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death.

verses.restored: For sin/misalignment, taking opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.

familiar.text: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.

verses.restored: So then, the Law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous/just and good.

familiar.text: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

verses.restored: Did the good become death to me? May it not be. But sin/misalignment, so that it might appear as sin/misalignment, was working death to me through the good, so that sin/misalignment through the commandment might become exceedingly sinful/misaligned.

familiar.text: Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.

verses.restored: For we know that the Law is spiritual; but I am fleshly, having been sold under sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

verses.restored: For what I work out, I do not know; for I do not practice what I will, but what I hate, this I do.

familiar.text: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.

verses.restored: But if what I do not will, this I do, I agree with the Law that it is beautiful/good.

familiar.text: If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.

verses.restored: Now then it is no longer I working it out, but sin/misalignment dwelling in me.

familiar.text: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

verses.restored: For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh; for to will is present with me, but to work out the beautiful/good is not.

familiar.text: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.

verses.restored: For the good that I will, I do not do; but the harmful thing I do not will, this I practice.

familiar.text: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.

verses.restored: But if what I do not will, this I do, it is no longer I working it out, but sin/misalignment dwelling in me.

familiar.text: Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

verses.restored: I find then the law/principle: when I will to do the beautiful/good, the harmful is present with me.

familiar.text: I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.

verses.restored: For I delight in the Law of the Divine according to the inner human,

familiar.text: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

verses.restored: but I see another law/principle in my members warring against the law/principle of my mind and taking me captive in the law/principle of sin/misalignment that is in my members.

familiar.text: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

verses.restored: Wretched human that I am. Who will rescue me from the body of this death?

familiar.text: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?

verses.restored: Thanks to the Divine through Jesus Messiah our Lord. So then, I myself with the mind serve the Law of the Divine, but with the flesh the law/principle of sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

translation_notes: Romans 7 does not call Torah evil. The Law is holy; sin/misalignment is the parasitic power that exploits commandment.
The divided I may be read as rhetorical, autobiographical, Adamic, Israel-under-Law, or existential; the restored layer preserves the ambiguity.
